subtitle: Buy the actuator. Engineer the interface.
description: A mounting cradle and simplified thruster envelope support early integration. The motor, pump, piston and seal internals are deliberately not released as manufacturable designs.
targets: RFQ starting point, not supplier selection
decisions: Buy an industrial thruster for the first brake prototypes.
Keep mounting clevises replaceable to adapt to the selected supplier drawing.
Separate thrust, stroke and time requirements; one cannot substitute for another.
materials: Thruster body and rod: supplier-controlled; CAD volumes are reserved space only.
risks: Force requirement cannot be finalized until the brake linkage is solved.
No internal hydraulic/electrical design, pressure rating or environmental certification.
steps: Replace envelope with supplier STEP and approved pin dimensions.
Fit cradle and retained pivots; inspect alignment across full stroke.
validation: Supplier documentation review and incoming force/stroke/time tests.
Side-load, mounting fatigue, seal leakage and temperature tests.
hypotheses: Compare integration effort with a quoted custom-thruster programme.
Verify access without dismantling the brake frame.
sensors: Specify motor voltage/frequency, duty cycle, insulation, cable entry, ingress, thermal protection and end-state sensing.
